title: Glessner's northeast courtyard corner gets its low copper roof and dormer
items: The courtyard corner between the dining bay and the round hall bay was copper laid flat on the tiles. It is now a low copper roof: the wall below stands higher, the copper runs flatter than the tiles above and meets them in a crease, its west end is hipped, and a downpipe stands at that corner. The 1963 survey's section and the aerial photographs both show it.
A small pointed dormer with a finial now sits on the slope just east of the great chimney, where the aerials and a 1923 photograph show one.
